answer: Coordination Depth Pricing.** Each identity’s ability to open new channels is rate-limited by the graph distance between the counterparties it cites, measured as discounted path length. Opening a channel across a willow of existing trust edges costs a fee proportional to the square of that distance, so cheap adjacent links stay cheap while distant ones climb toward a bridge premium. An attacker must pay repeatedly to connect fresh clusters, and the price rises as the network’s nadir of verified paths deepens;
